passage:
An online course gave students badges for finishing lessons. Kevin collected many badges quickly, but he skipped practice exercises.
When he tried to use the skill in a real project, he could not do it well.
His mentor said badges showed activity, not mastery. Kevin returned to the lessons and practiced slowly.
The badges were not useless. They helped track progress. But they were signs, not proof.
In learning, finishing content is not the same as understanding it. A badge can mark the path walked, but the skill must still be built in the hands and mind.
